original_value: AbstractIn virtual worlds (VWs), users have more VW games alternatives, whereas VW companies consequently suffer from high customer turnover rate and low customer loyalty. Therefore, building a churn prediction model to facilitate subsequent churn management and customer retention is important. The churn behaviours and the impact of social neighbour influences to customer churn may be different for different types of users. Accordingly, we segment users into stable, unstable, and solitary user groups according to their social contact behaviours in VWs. Novel segmentation‐based churn prediction approaches are proposed for churn prediction in VWs by building prediction models for each type of user groups and considering the effect of social neighbour influences for different user groups. The proposed approaches are evaluated by conducting experiments with a dataset collected from a VW platform. The experimental results show different churn prediction performances under different user groups. The segmentation‐based churn prediction approaches perform better than do general approaches without considering user groups. Moreover, the results also reveal that social neighbour influences have a positive impact on stable and unstable users. The proposed work contributes to investigating the social neighbour influences on churn prediction for different types of user groups in VWs.

result.paraphrase: In virtual worlds, users have many game alternatives, which leads VW companies to face high customer turnover and low loyalty. To support churn management and retention, a churn prediction model is needed. Since churn behavior and the impact of social neighbor influence can vary by user type, users are divided into stable, unstable, and solitary groups based on their social contact patterns in VWs. The paper proposes segmentation-based churn prediction methods that build separate prediction models for each user group and account for social neighbor effects by group. These methods are tested experimentally using data collected from a VW platform. The results show that churn prediction performance differs across user groups, and the segmentation-based methods outperform general approaches that ignore group structure. The findings also indicate that social neighbor influence positively affects stable and unstable users. Overall, the work helps examine social neighbor influences on churn prediction for different user groups in VWs.
